Subject: Possible exposure affecting tokens stored via subprocessor

Hi Evelyn,

We detected anomalous outbound connections from an integration that pulls inference logs and KV cache snapshots from your dedicated customer connector (vendor: DataBridgeX). Right now we are treating this as a potential data exposure affecting a small set of tokens and a handful of user identifiers — GammaHealth internal investigation is ongoing.

Per our DPA Section 6 (Notification and Cooperation), we are notifying processors and their subprocessors. Please see the attached initial packet with the observed indicators and a ticket (INCD-4421) we opened on our side. We need to understand:
- Whether Redwood treated DataBridgeX as a subprocessor for GammaHealth workloads and the contractual notice timing for subprocessor security events.
- What evidence retention window you have for requestable logs and how quickly you can deliver redacted artifacts for forensic review.

We appreciate a response within 48 hours so we can align on external notifications.

Thanks,
Robert Mills

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Evelyn — quick summary from infra:
- We do not push any KV cache snapshots off-platform to DataBridgeX for hosted customers. However, for Dedicated customers (GammaHealth is on Dedicated), there are optional connector jobs that can export anonymized sampling to third-party analytics; I need to confirm whether GammaHealth enabled that.
- Retention: runtime request logs (metadata only) are retained for 30 days by default; detailed request bodies and KV cache are purged after 7 days unless a retention extension is configured. We can produce redacted logs within 48 hours if we prioritize the ticket; full unredacted artifacts will need legal approval and may require an evidence-transfer agreement.

I'll run a query against the GammaHealth tenant (safe-mode) and report back within 6 hours. If it's a Dedicated-managed connector, we may have S3 object names and can generate a tarball of redacted artifacts (expected size small).

— Dev

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Possible exposure affecting tokens stored via subprocessor

Evelyn / Dev — legal guidance and proposed communication plan:
1) DPA obligations: our standard DPA (v3.1) requires us to notify the Controller (GammaHealth) "without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours" of becoming aware of a qualifying incident. For incidents that involve a subprocessor, our contracts require us to:
   - notify the Controller of any changes to subprocessors (irrelevant here)
   - cooperate and provide reasonable assistance for forensic review and regulatory obligations
2) Notification timing: GammaHealth's request for response in 48 hours is reasonable operationally. We should acknowledge receipt within 4 hours and provide a targeted update within 48 hours that includes scope (what data types were affected), initial remediation steps, and expected time to evidence delivery.
3) Evidence transfer: before sending unredacted logs we should:
   - execute a short evidence transfer agreement (ETA) or use the existing DPA exhibit that permits limited disclosures to Controller investigators (we have a precedent template).
   - redact PII that is not required for GammaHealth's forensic objectives; document redaction rules.
   - log and timestamp all artifacts we share.
4) Subprocessor obligations: if DataBridgeX is named as a subprocessor in our records for the GammaHealth tenant, we must also notify GammaHealth in writing and provide details of any actions we took regarding that subprocessor. If it is an independent third-party called by GammaHealth (not in our subprocessor chain), we should say so clearly.

Proposed immediate replies:
- Acknowledge receipt to GammaHealth within 4 hours.
- Confirm we are investigating and will provide a substantive update within 48 hours with an ETA for redacted artifacts.

I'll draft both the acknowledgement and the 48-hour update. Dev: please attach the list of object keys and a short description of the artifacts you can produce so I can prepare the ETA template.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

What we can confirm now:
- We are investigating and have prioritized this under ticket INCD-4421.
- At this point we believe GammaHealth’s Dedicated tenant may have an optional export connector enabled that writes sampling artifacts to a third-party bucket (we are querying that configuration). Dev will provide a list of object keys and a timeline for redacted artifacts within 24 hours.
- Per our DPA, Redwood’s standard notification window is 72 hours for qualifying incidents, but we will provide a substantive operational update within 48 hours as requested.

Next steps we propose:
1) We will produce a redacted artifact set (redacted_kvlogs.tar.gz) for GammaHealth investigators under our ETA; delivery ETA: 48–72 hours pending approvals.
2) We will confirm whether DataBridgeX is a Redwood-designated subprocessor for the GammaHealth workload or an external connector GammaHealth configured. If DataBridgeX is our subprocessor, we will include our actions regarding them in our update.
3) We will log all artifact transfers and preserve a full chain-of-custody record.

Please confirm if GammaHealth requires a specific evidence-transfer template or additional assurances on redaction rules. We will escalate to legal for expedited sign-off if needed.
